pattern.title: Probability
pattern.description: Classical probability across coins, dice, cards and bags.

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 3 head(s)?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes = 5C3 = 10. Total = 2^5 = 32. Probability = 5/16.
questions.shortcut: P = nCk / 2^n.

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 4 head(s)?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes = 5C4 = 5. Total = 2^5 = 32. Probability = 5/32.
questions.shortcut: P = nCk / 2^n.

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 head(s)?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes = 5C2 = 10. Total = 2^5 = 32. Probability = 5/16.
questions.shortcut: P = nCk / 2^n.

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 1 head(s)?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes = 3C1 = 3. Total = 2^3 = 8. Probability = 3/8.
questions.shortcut: P = nCk / 2^n.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers equals 3?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 2 have a sum that equals 3. Probability = 2/36 = 1/18.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers equals 6?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 5 have a sum that equals 6. Probability = 5/36 = 5/36.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is at most 3?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 3 have a sum that is at most 3. Probability = 3/36 = 1/12.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is at most 6?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 15 have a sum that is at most 6. Probability = 15/36 = 5/12.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers equals 5?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 4 have a sum that equals 5. Probability = 4/36 = 1/9.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers equals 10?
questions.explanation: Out of 36 equally likely outcomes, 3 have a sum that equals 10. Probability = 3/36 = 1/12.
questions.shortcut: List pairs by sum; total outcomes = 36.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is a multiple of 6?
questions.explanation: Counting the pairs (a, b) whose product is a multiple of 6: 15 out of 36. Probability = 5/12.
questions.shortcut: Count favourable pairs among the 36 outcomes.

questions.questionText: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is even?
questions.explanation: Counting the pairs (a, b) whose product is even: 27 out of 36. Probability = 3/4.
questions.shortcut: Count favourable pairs among the 36 outcomes.

questions.questionText: One card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a black card that is not a face card?
questions.explanation: There are 20 such cards out of 52. Probability = 20/52 = 5/13.
questions.shortcut: Favourable cards / 52.

questions.questionText: One card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting an ace?
questions.explanation: There are 4 such cards out of 52. Probability = 4/52 = 1/13.
questions.shortcut: Favourable cards / 52.

questions.questionText: One card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a red face card?
questions.explanation: There are 6 such cards out of 52. Probability = 6/52 = 3/26.
questions.shortcut: Favourable cards / 52.

questions.questionText: One card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a face card?
questions.explanation: There are 12 such cards out of 52. Probability = 12/52 = 3/13.
questions.shortcut: Favourable cards / 52.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both kings?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 4C2 = 6. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 1/221.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both aces?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 4C2 = 6. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 1/221.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both face cards?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 12C2 = 66. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 11/221.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both red cards?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 26C2 = 325. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 25/102.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both spades?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 13C2 = 78. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 1/17.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability that they are both hearts?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 13C2 = 78. Total = 52C2 = 1326. Probability = 1/17.
questions.shortcut: Use combinations: favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability of getting at least one ace?
questions.explanation: Total ways = 52C2 = 1326. Counting the favourable pairs for 'at least one ace' gives probability 33/221.
questions.shortcut: Count favourable pairs (or use the complement) over 52C2.

questions.questionText: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a pack of 52. What is the probability of getting one king and one queen?
questions.explanation: Total ways = 52C2 = 1326. Counting the favourable pairs for 'one king and one queen' gives probability 8/663.
questions.shortcut: Count favourable pairs (or use the complement) over 52C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 2 black, 7 green and 4 red balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 4, total = 13. Probability = 4/13.
questions.shortcut: Favourable / total.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 6 white, 6 black and 6 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is white?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 6, total = 18. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Favourable / total.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 3 black, 7 blue and 6 white balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 7, total = 16. Probability = 7/16.
questions.shortcut: Favourable / total.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 5 black, 4 white and 5 red balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 5, total = 14. Probability = 5/14.
questions.shortcut: Favourable / total.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 3 blue, 3 black and 5 red balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are blue?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 3 blue balls out of 11: 3C2/11C2 = 3/55 = 3/55.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 7 red, 3 blue and 2 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are black?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 2 black balls out of 12: 2C2/12C2 = 1/66 = 1/66.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 7 green, 5 white and 4 red balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are green?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 7 green balls out of 16: 7C2/16C2 = 21/120 = 7/40.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 6 black, 2 green and 3 red balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are black?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 6 black balls out of 11: 6C2/11C2 = 15/55 = 3/11.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 5 blue, 6 black and 6 white balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are black?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 6 black balls out of 17: 6C2/17C2 = 15/136 = 15/136.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 3 red, 6 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are white?
questions.explanation: Choose both balls from the 6 white balls out of 15: 6C2/15C2 = 15/105 = 1/7.
questions.shortcut: Both same colour: nC2 / total C2.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 3 red, 3 white and 4 green balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that one ball of each colour is drawn?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 3 x 3 x 4 = 36. Total = 10C3 = 120. Probability = 3/10.
questions.shortcut: One of each: multiply the counts, divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 6 blue, 6 red and 6 black balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that one ball of each colour is drawn?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 6 x 6 x 6 = 216. Total = 18C3 = 816. Probability = 9/34.
questions.shortcut: One of each: multiply the counts, divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: A bag contains 4 black, 2 white and 6 red balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that one ball of each colour is drawn?
questions.explanation: Favourable = 4 x 2 x 6 = 48. Total = 12C3 = 220. Probability = 12/55.
questions.shortcut: One of each: multiply the counts, divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: Two people are chosen at random from a group of 3 men and 5 women. What is the probability that both are men?
questions.explanation: Choose both people from the 3 men among 8 people: 3C2/8C2 = 3/28 = 3/28.
questions.shortcut: Favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two people are chosen at random from a group of 5 men and 3 women. What is the probability that both are men?
questions.explanation: Choose both people from the 5 men among 8 people: 5C2/8C2 = 10/28 = 5/14.
questions.shortcut: Favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word FLOWER are arranged at random. What is the probability that the resulting arrangement starts with a vowel?
questions.explanation: 2 of the 6 letters are vowels, so by symmetry P = 2/6 = 1/3 (checked by counting 240 of 720 arrangements).
questions.shortcut: First-letter probability = (vowels)/(letters).

questions.questionText: The letters of the word ORANGE are arranged at random. What is the probability that the resulting arrangement starts with a vowel?
questions.explanation: 3 of the 6 letters are vowels, so by symmetry P = 3/6 = 1/2 (checked by counting 360 of 720 arrangements).
questions.shortcut: First-letter probability = (vowels)/(letters).

questions.questionText: The letters of the word DELHI are arranged at random. What is the probability that the resulting arrangement starts with a vowel?
questions.explanation: 2 of the 5 letters are vowels, so by symmetry P = 2/5 = 2/5 (checked by counting 48 of 120 arrangements).
questions.shortcut: First-letter probability = (vowels)/(letters).

questions.questionText: Two people are chosen at random from a group of 3 men and 3 women. What is the probability that both are men?
questions.explanation: Choose both people from the 3 men among 6 people: 3C2/6C2 = 3/15 = 1/5.
questions.shortcut: Favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: Two people are chosen at random from a group of 7 men and 5 women. What is the probability that both are men?
questions.explanation: Choose both people from the 7 men among 12 people: 7C2/12C2 = 21/66 = 7/22.
questions.shortcut: Favourable pairs / total pairs.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 8?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 8 among them: 11. Probability = 11/90 = 11/90.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word SIGNAL are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Arrangements with the vowels together = 240. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 7?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 7 among them: 13. Probability = 13/90 = 13/90.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 9 among them: 10. Probability = 10/90 = 1/9.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 5?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 5 among them: 18. Probability = 18/90 = 1/5.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word LEADER are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 360. Arrangements with the vowels together = 72. Probability = 1/5.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word PLANET are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Arrangements with the vowels together = 240. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word CHANGE are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Arrangements with the vowels together = 240. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word WINDOW are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 360. Arrangements with the vowels together = 120. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 4?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 4 among them: 22. Probability = 22/90 = 11/45.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 12?
questions.explanation: There are 90 two-digit numbers. Multiples of 12 among them: 8. Probability = 8/90 = 4/45.
questions.shortcut: Count multiples in the range, divide by 90.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word MARKET are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Arrangements with the vowels together = 240. Probability = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word ORANGE are arranged at random. What is the probability that all the vowels come together?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Arrangements with the vowels together = 144. Probability = 1/5.
questions.shortcut: Vowel block as one unit, times the internal arrangements.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word LEADER are arranged at random. What is the probability that the resulting arrangement begins and ends with a consonant?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 360. Those beginning and ending with a consonant = 72. Probability = 1/5.
questions.shortcut: Choose the end letters first, then arrange the middle.

questions.questionText: A committee of 3 is chosen at random from 6 men and 3 women. What is the probability that it has exactly 2 women?
questions.explanation: Total = 9C3 = 84. Favourable = 18. Probability = 3/14.
questions.shortcut: Count by gender split; divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: The letters of the word CHANGE are arranged at random. What is the probability that the resulting arrangement begins and ends with a consonant?
questions.explanation: Total arrangements = 720. Those beginning and ending with a consonant = 288. Probability = 2/5.
questions.shortcut: Choose the end letters first, then arrange the middle.

questions.questionText: A committee of 3 is chosen at random from 6 men and 5 women. What is the probability that it has at least 1 woman?
questions.explanation: Total = 11C3 = 165. Favourable = 145. Probability = 29/33.
questions.shortcut: Count by gender split; divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: A committee of 3 is chosen at random from 4 men and 3 women. What is the probability that it has exactly 2 women?
questions.explanation: Total = 7C3 = 35. Favourable = 12. Probability = 12/35.
questions.shortcut: Count by gender split; divide by total C3.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/8 and P(B) = 1/5. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 1/8 x 1/5 = 1/40.
questions.shortcut: Independent: multiply.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/10 and P(B) = 3/10. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 1/10 x 3/10 = 3/100.
questions.shortcut: Independent: multiply.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/5 and P(B) = 1/5. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 1/5 x 1/5 = 1/25.
questions.shortcut: Independent: multiply.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/6 and P(B) = 1/3. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 1/6 x 1/3 = 1/18.
questions.shortcut: Independent: multiply.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/2 and P(B) = 2/5. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/6 and P(B) = 1/9. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 3/5 and P(B) = 2/3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 3/8 and P(B) = 1/5. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/10 and P(B) = 2/3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 1/8 and P(B) = 2/5. What is P(A or B)?
questions.shortcut: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

questions.questionText: For two events A and B, P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 2/9 and P(A or B) = 67/180. What is P(A and B)?
questions.shortcut: Inclusion-exclusion rearranged.

questions.questionText: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 3/8 and P(B) = 3/10. What is the probability that exactly one of them occurs?
questions.shortcut: Exactly one = A without B + B without A.

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 6 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: P(no head) = 1/2^6 = 1/64. P(at least one head) = 1 - 1/64 = 63/64.
questions.shortcut: At least one = 1 - P(none).

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 2 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: P(no head) = 1/2^2 = 1/4. P(at least one head) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.
questions.shortcut: At least one = 1 - P(none).

questions.questionText: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: P(no head) = 1/2^5 = 1/32. P(at least one head) = 1 - 1/32 = 31/32.
questions.shortcut: At least one = 1 - P(none).

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 2 times. What is the probability of getting at least one even number?
questions.explanation: P(no even number in a roll) = 1/2. For 2 rolls: (1/2)^2 = 1/4. P(at least one) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least one number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: P(no number greater than 4 in a roll) = 2/3. For 3 rolls: (2/3)^3 = 8/27. P(at least one) = 1 - 8/27 = 19/27.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 4 times. What is the probability of getting at least one number less than 3?
questions.explanation: P(no number less than 3 in a roll) = 2/3. For 4 rolls: (2/3)^4 = 16/81. P(at least one) = 1 - 16/81 = 65/81.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 2 times. What is the probability of getting at least one number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: P(no number greater than 4 in a roll) = 2/3. For 2 rolls: (2/3)^2 = 4/9. P(at least one) = 1 - 4/9 = 5/9.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least one even number?
questions.explanation: P(no even number in a roll) = 1/2. For 3 rolls: (1/2)^3 = 1/8. P(at least one) = 1 - 1/8 = 7/8.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 2 times. What is the probability of getting at least one six?
questions.explanation: P(no six in a roll) = 5/6. For 2 rolls: (5/6)^2 = 25/36. P(at least one) = 1 - 25/36 = 11/36.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled 4 times. What is the probability of getting at least one even number?
questions.explanation: P(no even number in a roll) = 1/2. For 4 rolls: (1/2)^4 = 1/16. P(at least one) = 1 - 1/16 = 15/16.
questions.shortcut: Use the complement: 1 - (probability of failing each time)^n.

questions.questionText: Three persons A, B and C try to hit a target independently with probabilities 3/8, 3/10 and 1/4 respectively. What is the probability that the target is hit by at least one of them?
questions.shortcut: 1 - product of the miss probabilities.

questions.questionText: Three persons A, B and C try to hit a target independently with probabilities 1/7, 1/9 and 1/10 respectively. What is the probability that the target is hit by at least one of them?
questions.shortcut: 1 - product of the miss probabilities.

questions.questionText: Three persons A, B and C try to hit a target independently with probabilities 1/6, 1/6 and 1/2 respectively. What is the probability that the target is hit by at least one of them?
questions.shortcut: 1 - product of the miss probabilities.

questions.questionText: The odds in favour of an event are 5:8. What is the probability that the event occurs?
questions.explanation: Probability = favourable/(favourable + unfavourable) = 5/(5 + 8) = 5/13.
questions.shortcut: Odds a:b in favour -> probability a/(a+b).

questions.questionText: The odds in favour of an event are 3:5. What is the probability that the event occurs?
questions.explanation: Probability = favourable/(favourable + unfavourable) = 3/(3 + 5) = 3/8.
questions.shortcut: Odds a:b in favour -> probability a/(a+b).

questions.questionText: The odds in favour of an event are 2:5. What is the probability that the event occurs?
questions.explanation: Probability = favourable/(favourable + unfavourable) = 2/(2 + 5) = 2/7.
questions.shortcut: Odds a:b in favour -> probability a/(a+b).

questions.questionText: The odds in favour of an event are 1:2. What is the probability that the event occurs?
questions.explanation: Probability = favourable/(favourable + unfavourable) = 1/(1 + 2) = 1/3.
questions.shortcut: Odds a:b in favour -> probability a/(a+b).

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 7/15. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 7:8, so odds against = 8:7 = 8:7.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 2/5. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 2:3, so odds against = 3:2 = 3:2.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 2/3. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 2:1, so odds against = 1:2 = 1:2.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 3/20. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 3:17, so odds against = 17:3 = 17:3.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 1/4. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 1:3, so odds against = 3:1 = 3:1.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: The probability of an event is 1/20. What are the odds against the event? (give as against : in favour)
questions.explanation: Odds in favour = 1:19, so odds against = 19:1 = 19:1.
questions.shortcut: Odds against = (1 - p) : p.

questions.questionText: A player rolls a die and wins Rs 50 if the number is a 5 or a 6; otherwise he loses Rs 10. What is his expected gain per roll (in Rs)?
questions.explanation: P(win) = 1/3. Expected gain = 1/3 x 50 - 2/3 x 10 = 10.
questions.shortcut: Expected value = sum of (outcome x probability).

questions.questionText: A player rolls a die and wins Rs 80 if the number is 6; otherwise he loses Rs 10. What is his expected gain per roll (in Rs)?
questions.explanation: P(win) = 1/6. Expected gain = 1/6 x 80 - 5/6 x 10 = 5.
questions.shortcut: Expected value = sum of (outcome x probability).

questions.questionText: A player rolls a die and wins Rs 60 if the number is 6; otherwise he loses Rs 10. What is his expected gain per roll (in Rs)?
questions.explanation: P(win) = 1/6. Expected gain = 1/6 x 60 - 5/6 x 10 = 5/3.
questions.shortcut: Expected value = sum of (outcome x probability).
